subject.title: fix(codex): heartbeat notifications to other channels are silently denied by cross-context policy

question: Should internal WebChat-marked heartbeat, cron, and inter-session Codex turns be treated as unbound autonomous contexts that may send across providers under the default policy?
rationale: The code and proof support the proposed distinction, but removing a provider binding changes the authorization context for autonomous messaging and repository evidence cannot establish the intended trust model without owner intent.

options.title: Approve scoped autonomous unbinding
options.body: Accept the PR's narrow classifier, retain bindings for genuine WebChat and real-channel turns, refresh onto current main, and land after focused routing proof.

options.title: Require explicit cross-provider authorization
options.body: Keep internal turns bound by default and introduce a separately approved capability or policy signal for autonomous cross-provider notifications.

options.title: Preserve current containment
options.body: Decline the behavior change and document that operators must opt into cross-provider sends, accepting that the reported default workflow remains broken.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped autonomous unbinding
recommendation.body: Accept the PR's narrow classifier, retain bindings for genuine WebChat and real-channel turns, refresh onto current main, and land after focused routing proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged-history provenance is the internal-turn message registration work credited to this person in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93813.
